A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana issued notice to Meta and X (formerly Twitter) and sought responses from them. However, while issuing notice, the Court flagged the difficulty in regulating content once it enters the digital ecosystem. “Issue notice. items.title: Kerala HC flags misuse of POCSO Act in marital disputes; clears man accused of raping stepdaughter
items.summary: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act) is prone to misuse by some sections of people to wreak vengeance during times of matrimonial discord, cautioned the Kerala High Court recently. Justice A Badharudeen made the observation while acquitting a man accused of sexually assaulting his stepdaughter. The Court found there were several factors that raised doubts about the genuineness of the allegations in this case. The question of whether the accused was falsely accused by his estranged wife could not be ruled out, it concluded. "The provisions of the POCSO Act have been misused by a section of people to wreak vengeance, settle scores and obtain illegal gain. The prime area where one could find false implication of innocent persons in POCSO cases is when there is matrimonial discord between two spouses," it observed. items.title: News report on person's arrest not defamation: Kerala HC quashes case against Manorama editor
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently held that a news report about a person's arrest does not constitute the offence of criminal defamation merely on the ground that it caused embarrassment to the person arrested [ Mammen Mathew & Ors. v. State of Kerala & Anr. ] Justice CS Dias made the observation while quashing a criminal defamation case against the Chief Editor of Malayala Manorama, one of its editors and a reporter who were booked over a news report in the Malayalam news daily. The Court emphasised that the distinction between a report of an official proceeding such as an arrest and an independent defamatory assertion is crucial to decide a claim of defamation. The Court noted that when faithful reportage of court proceedings is protected from defamation claims under the Indian Penal Code, there is no ground to justify adding a defamatory intent to a substantially accurate report on the registration of a crime or arrest of an accused.
